assumptions.assumption: Players with NULL bats are kept as their own group (the request excludes only empty strings), but the condition p.bats <> '' also drops NULL bats rows, so NULL-bats players are excluded as well.
Inner join on player_id; each appearances row counts as one appearance record, and player_id is assumed unique in player.
The total and the average group count are computed over the remaining batting-hand groups only (after dropping empty-string bats).

assumptions.assumption: Players whose bats is NULL are dropped along with the empty-string ones, because the filter bats <> '' is not true for NULL. The request names only the empty string, so keeping NULL as its own group is a possible reading.
The ratios are computed as non-integer values: COUNT(*) is multiplied by 1.0 so the division is not integer division. Nothing is rounded.
Each appearances row counts once. The inner join to player is on player_id, and player_id is assumed unique in player, so rows are not duplicated.
